title: API Versioning Strategy
content: Our API versioning strategy uses URL path versioning (v1, v2) with a minimum 12-month backward compatibility window. Breaking changes require a new major version. Deprecation notices are published 6 months before removal. All API responses include a Sunset header when accessing deprecated endpoints. Client libraries are updated within 2 weeks of a new version release.

title: Deployment and Rollback Procedure
content: Deployments follow a blue-green strategy with canary validation. Each deployment must pass health checks for 5 minutes before receiving production traffic. Rollback is triggered automatically if error rate exceeds 1% or p99 latency exceeds 500ms. Manual rollback is available via the ops dashboard. All deployments require two approvals and a linked ticket.

title: API Rate Limiting Policy
content: Rate limits are enforced per API key using a sliding window algorithm. Free tier: 100 requests per minute. Pro tier: 1000 requests per minute. Enterprise: custom limits negotiated per contract. Rate limit headers (X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset) are included in every response. Exceeding the limit returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header.

title: Code Review Standards
content: All code changes require at least one approval before merging. Security-sensitive changes require two approvals including a security team member. Reviews should be completed within 24 hours. Reviewers check for correctness, test coverage (minimum 80%), documentation, and adherence to style guidelines. Automated linting runs on every pull request.

title: Authentication Architecture
content: Authentication uses JWT tokens with RS256 signing. Access tokens expire after 15 minutes. Refresh tokens expire after 7 days and are rotated on each use. Token expiration is validated server-side on every request. Failed authentication attempts are rate-limited to 5 per minute per IP address. Multi-factor authentication is required for admin accounts.

title: API Design Guidelines
content: APIs follow REST conventions with JSON request and response bodies. Endpoints use plural nouns (e.g., /users, /documents). Filtering uses query parameters. Pagination uses cursor-based navigation with next_cursor tokens. Error responses follow RFC 7807 Problem Details format. All new endpoints must have OpenAPI specifications and integration tests before release. Backward compatibility is maintained across minor versions.

title: Infrastructure Scaling Policy
content: Auto-scaling is configured for all production services. CPU threshold: scale up at 70%, scale down at 30%. Minimum instances: 3 per region. Maximum instances: 50 per region. Rate limiting infrastructure scales independently from application services. Database connections are pooled with a maximum of 100 connections per instance. Scaling events are logged and reviewed weekly.

title: Security Token Management
content: API keys and authentication tokens are stored encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM. Token rotation is mandatory every 90 days for service accounts. Compromised tokens must be revoked within 1 hour of detection. Token expiration policies are enforced at the gateway level. All token operations are logged in the audit trail with actor, timestamp, and IP address.

title: Database Migration Process
content: Schema migrations are version-controlled and applied sequentially. Each migration must be reversible with a corresponding down migration. Migrations are tested against a production-like dataset before deployment. Large table alterations use online DDL tools to avoid locking. Migration approval requires database team sign-off for any change affecting tables with more than 1 million rows.

title: Monitoring and Alerting Standards
content: All services must expose health check endpoints (/healthz, /readyz) and Prometheus metrics. Alert thresholds: error rate above 0.1% triggers warning, above 1% triggers critical. Latency alerts fire when p99 exceeds 2x the baseline for 5 consecutive minutes. On-call engineers must acknowledge alerts within 15 minutes. Post-incident reviews are required for all severity 1 and 2 incidents.

title: Master Service Agreement Terms
content: The standard MSA includes a 30-day termination notice period for monthly contracts and 90 days for annual contracts. Early termination incurs a fee equal to 50% of remaining contract value. The agreement auto-renews for successive 12-month periods unless written notice is provided. Governing law is England and Wales. Dispute resolution follows arbitration under ICC rules.

title: Data Retention Policy
content: Personal data is retained for the duration of the service agreement plus 30 days. Transaction records are retained for 7 years per financial regulations. Log data is retained for 90 days. Backup data is retained for 30 days after deletion from primary storage. Data retention schedules are reviewed annually for compliance with GDPR, CCPA, and sector-specific requirements.

title: Intellectual Property Terms
content: All intellectual property created during the engagement is assigned to the client upon full payment. Pre-existing IP remains with the originating party and is licensed non-exclusively. The assignment clause covers patents, copyrights, trade secrets, and trademarks. Moral rights are waived to the extent permitted by law. Third-party open-source components are documented in a software bill of materials.

title: GDPR Compliance Framework
content: Data subject access requests (DSARs) must be fulfilled within 30 calendar days. The data protection officer reviews all DSARs within 48 hours of receipt. Data processing agreements are required with all sub-processors. Privacy impact assessments are mandatory for new features processing personal data. Data breach notification to the supervisory authority must occur within 72 hours of awareness.

title: Acceptable Use Policy
content: Prohibited uses include reverse engineering, competitive analysis, storing illegal content, cryptocurrency mining, and automated scraping without authorisation. Usage that exceeds 10x the contracted capacity triggers a fair-use review. Violations result in a warning, temporary suspension, or termination depending on severity. Appeals are handled by the trust and safety team within 5 business days.

title: Data Processing Agreement
content: The processor shall process personal data only on documented instructions from the controller. Sub-processing requires prior written consent. The processor must implement appropriate technical and organisational measures including encryption at rest and in transit. Data retention follows the controller's data retention policy. Annual compliance audits are permitted with 30 days notice.

title: Service Level Agreement
content: Monthly uptime target: 99.9%. Credits for downtime: 10% of monthly fee per 0.1% below target, capped at 30%. Planned maintenance windows: Sundays 02:00-06:00 UTC, excluded from uptime calculations. Termination notice period: 30 days for standard contracts, 90 days for enterprise agreements. Emergency maintenance may occur with 4 hours notice.

title: Privacy Notice
content: We collect account information, usage data, and device identifiers. Personal data is processed under legitimate interest (service delivery) and consent (marketing). Data subject rights include access, rectification, erasure, portability, and objection. DSAR requests are processed within 30 days. Data is stored in EU data centres. International transfers use Standard Contractual Clauses.

title: Contributor Licence Agreement
content: Contributors grant a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to use, modify, and distribute their contributions. The contributor represents they have the right to make the contribution. Intellectual property in contributions is assigned to the project maintainer. Moral rights are waived where legally permissible. The CLA covers all forms of contribution including code, documentation, and artwork.

title: Export Control Compliance
content: Software is classified under EAR 5D002 for cryptographic functionality. Export to sanctioned countries (Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Crimea) is prohibited. End-user screening against denied-parties lists is performed at registration. Encryption algorithms used: AES-256, RSA-2048, Ed25519, BLAKE3. Annual export compliance training is required for all engineering and sales staff.

title: Cloud Infrastructure Cost Allocation
content: Cloud costs are allocated to cost centres using resource tagging. Each team maintains tags for department, project, and environment. Untagged resources are charged to the engineering overhead budget. Monthly cost reviews are conducted by finance and engineering leads. Cost centre allocation for shared infrastructure (databases, load balancers, monitoring) uses a weighted usage model based on request volume.

title: Revenue Forecasting Model
content: Quarterly revenue forecasts use a bottom-up methodology combining pipeline-weighted deals, expansion revenue from existing customers, and historical churn rates. The forecast model is updated monthly with actual bookings data. Forecast accuracy is measured against actuals with a target variance of less than 10%. ARR growth projections assume 20% year-over-year expansion with 5% annual churn.

title: Budget Variance Reporting
content: Budget variance analysis is performed monthly for all cost centres. Variances exceeding 10% require written explanations from budget owners. Quarterly reforecasts adjust budgets based on actual spend patterns. The finance team publishes variance reports by the 10th business day of each month. Material variances (above 15%) trigger a review meeting with the CFO and department head.

title: Procurement Policy
content: Purchases under 1000 GBP require manager approval. Purchases between 1000 and 10000 GBP require director approval. Purchases above 10000 GBP require VP approval and a formal procurement process. Preferred vendors must be used unless a documented exception is approved. Payment terms are net-30 for standard vendors and net-60 for strategic partners.

title: Travel and Expense Policy
content: Business travel requires pre-approval from the department head. Economy class for flights under 6 hours; business class permitted for flights over 6 hours. Hotel rates capped at 200 GBP per night in London, 150 GBP elsewhere in the UK. Meal expenses: 50 GBP per day maximum. Receipts required for all expenses over 25 GBP. Expense approval thresholds: manager up to 500 GBP, director up to 2000 GBP.

title: Cloud Cost Optimisation Framework
content: Reserved instances cover 70% of baseline compute capacity. Spot instances used for batch processing and CI/CD workloads. Right-sizing reviews conducted quarterly using 30-day utilisation data. Idle resource detection runs weekly with automatic shutdown after 7 days of inactivity. Cloud cost centre allocation uses the direct-attribution model for dedicated resources and weighted-usage for shared services.

title: Financial Planning Process
content: Annual budget planning begins in Q3 with department submissions due by October 15th. Revenue forecasting methodology combines historical growth rates, pipeline analysis, and market benchmarks. Quarterly business reviews compare forecast to actuals with variance analysis. The rolling 12-month forecast is updated monthly. Capital expenditure requests above 50000 GBP require board approval.

title: Internal Audit Framework
content: Internal audits are conducted quarterly for financial controls and annually for operational processes. Budget variance thresholds trigger automatic audit review when sustained above 15% for two consecutive months. Audit findings are classified as critical (30-day remediation), major (60-day), or minor (90-day). The audit committee reviews all critical findings within one week of discovery.

title: Expense Reimbursement Process
content: Expense reports must be submitted within 30 days of the expense date. Reports are processed within 10 business days of approval. International expenses are converted at the exchange rate on the transaction date. Mileage reimbursement: 0.45 GBP per mile for the first 10000 miles, 0.25 GBP thereafter. Approval thresholds for travel expenses: line manager for under 500 GBP, department head for 500-2000 GBP, finance director above 2000 GBP.

title: Revenue Recognition Policy
content: Revenue is recognised in accordance with IFRS 15. Subscription revenue is recognised ratably over the contract period. Professional services revenue is recognised on completion of milestones. Hardware revenue is recognised at the point of delivery. Multi-element arrangements allocate revenue based on standalone selling prices. Contract modifications are treated as separate contracts when they add distinct goods or services.

title: ML Model Evaluation Protocol
content: Model evaluation uses a standardised pipeline: 70% training, 15% validation, 15% test split. Metrics include accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and AUC-ROC for classification tasks. Regression tasks use RMSE, MAE, and R-squared. All evaluation metrics are computed on the held-out test set. Cross-validation with 5 folds is required for models with fewer than 10000 training samples. Results must include confidence intervals.

title: Data Collection Ethics
content: All human-subjects research requires institutional review board approval before data collection begins. Informed consent must be obtained in writing. Participants may withdraw at any time without penalty. Personally identifiable information is pseudonymised at collection and stored separately from research data. Data sharing agreements must be in place before transferring data to collaborating institutions.

title: Statistical Analysis Standards
content: Hypothesis tests use a significance level of alpha equals 0.05 unless explicitly justified otherwise. Multiple comparison corrections (Bonferroni or Benjamini-Hochberg) are required when testing more than 3 hypotheses. Effect sizes must be reported alongside p-values. Sample size calculations must be documented before data collection. Statistical significance alone is insufficient for claiming a meaningful result; practical significance must also be assessed.

title: Peer Review Process
content: Internal peer review follows a double-blind protocol where both authors and reviewers are anonymised. Each manuscript requires two independent reviewers with relevant domain expertise. Reviewers have 14 days to complete their assessment. Review criteria include methodological rigour, novelty, clarity of presentation, and reproducibility. Conflicts of interest must be declared before accepting a review assignment.

title: Research Data Management
content: All research data must be stored in the institutional repository within 30 days of collection. Data is classified into three tiers: public (open access), restricted (authorised access), and confidential (encrypted storage only). Metadata must follow the Dublin Core standard. Research data sharing is required for publicly funded projects unless ethical constraints apply. Data reproducibility packages must include raw data, processing scripts, and environment specifications.

title: Benchmark Design Principles
content: Benchmarks must include a standardised evaluation framework with predefined metrics. Test datasets should be representative of real-world distributions. Baseline comparisons against at least two established methods are required. Machine learning model evaluation must report training time, inference latency, and memory usage alongside accuracy metrics. Benchmark results must be reproducible from published code and data.

title: Experimental Design Framework
content: Experiments follow a pre-registered protocol documenting hypotheses, methods, and analysis plans before data collection. Control groups are mandatory for comparative studies. Randomisation procedures are documented and verified. Statistical power analysis determines minimum sample sizes with a target power of 0.8 at the p-value threshold of 0.05. Negative results are documented and published with the same rigour as positive findings.

title: Citation Standards
content: All claims must be supported by primary sources published in peer-reviewed venues. Self-citation is limited to 20% of the reference list. Pre-print citations are permitted but must be flagged as non-peer-reviewed. Data citations must include persistent identifiers (DOI or equivalent). Citation metadata is verified against CrossRef or DataCite before submission. Retracted papers must not be cited as supporting evidence.

title: Publication Ethics Policy
content: Authorship follows the ICMJE criteria: substantial contributions to conception, drafting or revision, final approval, and accountability. Ghost authorship and honorary authorship are prohibited. Duplicate submission is not permitted. The peer review process is double-blind with anonymous reviewers and redacted author information. Plagiarism detection software is run on all submissions. Data fabrication or falsification results in immediate retraction and institutional notification.

title: Open Science Framework
content: Pre-registration of studies is encouraged for confirmatory research. Data availability statements are required in all publications. Code repositories must be archived with a DOI before publication. Reproducibility audits are conducted annually on a random sample of 10% of published studies. Research data sharing through institutional repositories enables verification and reuse. Open-access publication is mandated for publicly funded research within 12 months of acceptance.

title: Incident Classification Matrix
content: Severity 1 (Critical): Complete service outage affecting all users. Response time: 15 minutes. Resolution target: 4 hours. Severity 2 (Major): Significant degradation affecting more than 25% of users. Response time: 30 minutes. Resolution target: 8 hours. Severity 3 (Minor): Limited impact on a subset of features. Response time: 2 hours. Resolution target: 24 hours. Severity classification levels determine escalation path and communication cadence.

title: SLA Monitoring and Reporting
content: Service level agreements define uptime targets as a percentage of total minutes in the measurement period. Monthly uptime is calculated as: (total minutes minus downtime minutes) divided by total minutes times 100. Planned maintenance windows are excluded from SLA calculations. SLA reports are published by the 5th business day of each month. Uptime percentage calculation uses the agreed measurement methodology with 1-minute granularity sampling.

title: Change Management Process
content: All production changes follow the ITIL change management workflow. Standard changes: pre-approved, documented in the change catalogue. Normal changes: require CAB approval with 48 hours notice. Emergency changes: approved by the on-call manager with retrospective CAB review within 48 hours. Change approval workflow requires risk assessment, rollback plan, and testing evidence. Changes are scheduled during maintenance windows when possible.

title: Disaster Recovery Procedures
content: Recovery point objective (RPO): 1 hour for critical systems, 24 hours for non-critical. Recovery time objective (RTO): 4 hours for critical, 24 hours for non-critical. Database backups run hourly with point-in-time recovery capability. DR drills are conducted quarterly with full failover testing annually. Deployment rollback procedures are tested monthly. Geographic redundancy across two data centre regions ensures continuity.

title: Capacity Planning Framework
content: Capacity reviews are conducted monthly using 90-day trending data. CPU utilisation alerts trigger at 70% sustained for 15 minutes. Memory threshold alerts fire at 80% utilisation. Disk space warnings at 75%, critical at 90%. Capacity planning for memory and compute uses linear regression on historical usage with a 6-month planning horizon. Auto-scaling policies handle short-term demand spikes within pre-approved limits.

title: Incident Response Playbook
content: Incident response follows four phases: detection, triage, resolution, and post-mortem. Severity classification levels 1 through 4 determine response urgency and team composition. The incident commander coordinates response and communication. Status updates are posted every 30 minutes for Severity 1, hourly for Severity 2. Post-incident reviews are completed within 5 business days. Action items from reviews are tracked to completion.

title: Uptime Measurement Methodology
content: Uptime is measured using synthetic monitoring probes from three geographic regions. A service is considered down when two or more probes fail simultaneously. SLA uptime percentage is calculated monthly using minute-level resolution. Excluded from calculations: planned maintenance (with 48h notice), force majeure events, and customer-caused outages. The measurement method uses active health checks against the /readyz endpoint every 60 seconds.

title: Infrastructure Monitoring Standards
content: All production systems must have: CPU, memory, disk, and network utilisation monitoring with 1-minute resolution. Application-level metrics include request rate, error rate, and latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99). Capacity planning alerts for memory threshold at 80% utilisation. Database monitoring includes connection pool usage, query latency, and replication lag. Log aggregation with 90-day retention. Dashboards are reviewed weekly by the on-call team.

title: On-Call Rotation Policy
content: On-call rotations are weekly, Monday to Monday. Primary and secondary on-call engineers are designated for each rotation. Response time requirement: 15 minutes for Severity 1, 30 minutes for Severity 2. On-call engineers receive a weekly stipend and compensatory time off. Escalation path: primary on-call, secondary on-call, engineering manager, VP Engineering. Handoff meetings occur every Monday at 10:00 UTC.

title: Release Management Process
content: Releases follow a bi-weekly cadence with code freeze on Wednesday and deployment on Thursday. Hotfix releases may be deployed at any time with change management approval. Release candidates require sign-off from QA, security, and product teams. Change management approval is required for all production deployments. Release notes are published before deployment. Feature flags enable gradual rollout and instant rollback without redeployment.
